topic.name: The Intersection Between a Line and a Plane

question.text: Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations \[ l: \mathbf{r} = \langle 3,0,-4 \rangle + t \langle 2,4,3 \rangle, \qquad \Pi: 4x+3y+4z-60 = 0. \]
question.explanation:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as \[ \mathbf{r} = \langle 3+2t , 4t, -4+3t \rangle. \]

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

\begin{align*} 4x+3y+4z-60 &= 0 \\[3pt] 4x+3y+4z &= 60 \\[3pt] \langle x, y, z \rangle \cdot \langle 4, 3, 4 \rangle &= 60 \\[3pt] \mathbf{r}\cdot \langle 4, 3, 4 \rangle &= 60 \end{align*}

Now, substituting $\mathbf{r} = \langle 3+2t , 4t, -4+3t \rangle$ into the equation of the plane, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}\cdot \langle 4, 3, 4 \rangle &= 60 \\[3pt] \langle 3+2t , 4t, -4+3t \rangle \cdot \langle 4,3,4 \rangle &= 60 \\[3pt] 4(3+2t) + 3(4t) +4(-4 + 3t) &= 60 \\[3pt] 12+8t + 12t - 16 + 12t &= 60 \\[3pt] 32t &= 64 \\[3pt] t &= 2. \end{align*}

Finally, to get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{p} &= \langle 3+2(2), 4(2), -4+3(2) \rangle \\[3pt] &= \langle 7, 8, 2 \rangle \end{align*}

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(7, 8, 2).$

example.title: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line and a Plane Given in Other Forms

question.text: Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations \[ l:\mathbf{r} = \langle 4,1,6 \rangle + t \langle 2,6,0 \rangle, \qquad \Pi:\mathbf{r} \cdot \langle -24,8,6 \rangle = -32. \]
question.explanation:
Let's write the equation of the line as

\[ \mathbf{r} = \langle 4+2t , 1+6t, 6 \rangle. \]

Now, substituting $\mathbf{r} = \langle 4+2t , 1+6t, 6 \rangle$ into the equation of the plane, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r} \cdot \langle -24,8,6 \rangle &= -32 \\[3pt] \langle 4+2t , 1+6t, 6 \rangle \cdot \langle -24,8,6 \rangle &= -32 \\[3pt] -24(4+2t) + 8(1+6t) + 6\cdot6 &= -32 \\[3pt] -96-48t + 8+48t + 36 &= -32 \\[3pt] -52 &= -32. \end{align*}

The equation has no solution. Therefore, we conclude that the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ do not intersect.

example.title: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line in Vector Form and a Plane in Dot Product Form

question.text: Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations \[ l:\mathbf{r} = \langle 3,5,9 \rangle + t \langle 4,-1,6 \rangle, \qquad \Pi:-2x+4y+2z-16 = 0. \]
question.explanation:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as \[ \mathbf{r} = \langle 3+4t , 5-t, 9+6t \rangle. \]

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

\begin{align*} -2x+4y+2z-16 &= 0 \\[3pt] -2x+4y+2z &= 16 \\[3pt] \langle x, y, z \rangle \cdot \langle -2, 4, 2 \rangle &= 16 \\[3pt] \mathbf{r}\cdot \langle -2, 4, 2 \rangle &= 16 \end{align*}

Now, substituting $\mathbf{r} = \langle 3+4t , 5-t, 9+6t \rangle$ into the equation of the plane, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r} \cdot \langle -2, 4, 2 \rangle &= 16 \\[3pt] \langle 3+4t , 5-t, 9+6t \rangle \cdot \langle -2, 4, 2 \rangle &= 16 \\[3pt] -2(3+4t) + 4(5-t) + 2(9+6t) &= 16 \\[3pt] -6-8t + 20-4t + 18+12t &= 16 \\[3pt] 32 &= 16. \end{align*}

The equation has no solution. Therefore, we conclude that the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ do not intersect.

example.title: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line and a Plane Given in Other Forms

question.text: Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations \[ l: \begin{cases} x = -2-2t \\ y = 5-3t \\ z = -1+2t \end{cases} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \Pi:3x-2y+6z = 62. \]
question.explanation:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

\begin{align*} 3x-2y+6z &= 62 \\[3pt] 3(-2-2t) - 2(5-3t) + 6(-1+2t) &= 62 \\[3pt] -6-6t -10+6t - 6+12t &= 62 \\[3pt] 12t &= 84\\[3pt] t &= 7 \end{align*}

To get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=6$ into the parametric equations of the line:

\[ \begin{cases} x = -2-2(7) = -16 \\ y = 5-3(7) = -16 \\ z = -1+2(7) = 13 \end{cases} \]

So, the intersection point is $P(-16,-16,13).$

example.title: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line in Parametric Form and a Plane in Cartesian Form

question.text: Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations \[ l: \begin{cases} x = -3+t \\ y = -1+2t \\ z = 2+4t \end{cases} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \Pi:6x+4y+3z = 88. \]
question.explanation:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

\begin{align*} 6x+4y+3z &= 88 \\[3pt] 6(-3+t) + 4(-1+2t) + 3(2+4t) &= 88 \\[3pt] -18+6t - 4 + 8t + 6+12t &= 88 \\[3pt] 26t &= 104 \\[3pt] t &= 4 \end{align*}

To get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=4$ into the parametric equations of the line:

\[ \begin{cases} x = -3+4 = 1\\ y = -1+2(4) = 7\\ z = 2+4(4) = 18 \end{cases} \]

So, the intersection point is $P(1, 7, 18).$
